reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes laser and Joule heating synthesis of HEA nanoparticles on carbon supports, focusing on nucleation mechanisms and support graphitization. Neither passage provides data on differential atomic mobilities, surface segregation, local melting point reduction, or the effect of pre-annealing on melting onset in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited prior evidence.
premises: Differential atomic mobilities among Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, Cu lead to preferential surface segregation at high temperatures
Surface segregation creates regions with a reduced local melting point
This local melting point reduction nucleates a liquid-like layer (premelting) that propagates inward
Pre-annealing to homogenize elemental distribution suppresses or delays this segregation and melting onset
